fields.name: service_handle
fields.doc: Runtime-only: session images do not retain or reconstruct this handle.

ta_actor_active_states_params.doc: The active configuration: every active state, ancestors included, in document order. Resolve IDs with ta_definition_state().

ta_actor_capture_params.doc:
A session image is an owned in-memory representation of Tinyactors-managed interpreter state.  It is not a persistence wire format and does not contain the host-owned data-model object graph.  Host values referenced by interpreter-owned events, timers, or continuation state are retained as host references according to ta_value lifetime rules.

Invoker service handles are runtime-only and are not rebound.  Restoring an image retires every invocation that was active in it and appends one `error.communication.invoke. <id >.unavailable` platform event to the internal queue.  The event name identifies the invocation; its invoke_id field remains TA_INVOKE_ID_NONE because the event was generated by the processor, not the invoked service.  Those events follow internal events already captured by the image.  An active invocation therefore does not make capture or restoration return TA_ERR_NOT_RECONSTRUCTIBLE.

ta_actor_reconstruct() restores an image without participating in named routing. ta_actor_load() wraps the same reconstruction in the named-actor residency protocol and publishes it only when the directory still says UNLOADED. An image is still the host's to hold, to index by ta_session_image_next_deadline(), and to destroy.

An unpublished prepared replacement is not a routable session yet and cannot be captured; ta_actor_capture() returns TA_ERR_BUSY until activation.

ta_actor_completion.doc: Release data with ta_value_release() when has_data is true.

fields.name: actor
fields.doc: Meaningful only for TA_ACTOR_DIRECTORY_RESIDENT.

fields.name: claim
fields.doc: claim succeeds only when the address has no entry.

fields.name: replace
fields.doc: replace/remove are atomic comparisons against params->expected.

ta_actor_history_params.doc: The states recorded by one history pseudo-state, in document order. `*count` is zero when the history has never been recorded; its default transition then applies.

ta_actor_inspection.doc:
A read-only operational view of one resident interpreter instance.

Fixed-size facts are fields; the internal queue, the invocations and the delayed sends are borrowed arrays; the active configuration and history are read with the ta_actor_* list functions below, whose counts are reported here so a host can size buffers once. Inspecting one actor costs O(size of that actor), never O(size of the system) (ADR 0054).

Core pointers are borrowed and valid only while the actor is externally synchronized against mutation. The completion pointer and its data are borrowed and must not be released. Inspection never calls the data-model adapter; read the data model with ta_actor_datamodel_root().

fields.name: active_state_count
fields.doc: Number of states in the active configuration, ancestors included.

fields.name: macrostep_in_progress
fields.doc: True while a macrostep is paused mid-way (ta_actor_resume() continues it).

fields.name: current_event
fields.doc: The external event of the paused macrostep, or null.

fields.name: delayed_sends
fields.doc: Pending delayed sends, ordered by due time, then send order.

fields.name: allocated_bytes
fields.doc: Bytes the core currently allocates for this actor: the actor record, session storage (configuration and history), the data-model instance, sparse state, and queue capacities. Excludes memory the data-model adapter allocates itself. A measurement: it may change between releases.

ta_arena_block.doc:
======================================================================== Arenas

A growable bump allocator over a ta_allocator. Adapters and hosts may use it for request- or definition-scoped storage; it performs no I/O and frees everything at reset or destroy.

ta_chart_codec_info.doc: What a codec is, for a host choosing one and a tool reporting what it did. Every field is fixed for the codec's lifetime.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The representation this codec reads and writes: the registered media type where one exists ("application/scxml+xml"), otherwise a stable identifier of the implementer's choosing. It is also what a decode writes into a literal content's media_type.

fields.name: extensions
fields.doc: Conventional file extensions without the dot, terminated by an empty one; absent when the representation has none.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: One line, for a tool's --help.

fields.name: decode
fields.doc:
Decode `input` into a spec.

**The spec may point into `input`.** A codec is not required to copy, because a codec over a syntax tree keeps expression text as exact slices of the source, which is what lets an embedder map a compiled expression back to the construct it came from and run static checks on it before compiling. So `input` must stay valid as long as the spec does — until ta_definition_compile_spec() has copied it. Callers keep the buffer; codecs that do copy make that harmless.

A codec bounds its own input: nesting depth, document size, expansion. Reaching one of its bounds is TA_CHART_ERROR_LIMIT. The interface sets no bound of its own, so two codecs need not accept the same documents.

A literal <content > is decoded to bytes plus this codec's `info.name` as their media type. What those bytes are is the codec's rule: an XML codec serializes the content subtree with namespaces resolved as SCXML G.6 requires, rather than slicing the source, because what a recipient must see is a re-serialization and not the author's bytes.

TA_OK, TA_ERR_INVALID with `error` saying why, or TA_ERR_NOMEM. Null when this codec only writes.

fields.name: encode
fields.doc: Write `spec` in this codec's syntax. `spec->identity` is not written: identity has no chart syntax, so a round trip that must preserve an explicit one carries it beside the document and feeds it back through ta_chart_decode_params. A literal content whose media type is not this codec's own is TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE unless the codec can carry it verbatim. Null when this codec only reads.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: The operation's arena. Everything the decode allocates lives here — the codec's own parse, the spec, and the transients in between — and nothing outlives it. Reset or destroy it once the spec is compiled.

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: No chart syntax has a form for a definition's identity, so it is supplied here or not at all; absent means the compiler fingerprints.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: The operation's arena: the output bytes and everything the encode needed to produce them.

fields.name: construct
fields.doc: the element or production the error is about

fields.name: attribute
fields.doc: empty when it is not about one

fields.name: message
fields.doc: a fixed phrase owned by the codec

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_SYNTAX
constants.doc: not well-formed in this codec's syntax

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_NOT_CHART
constants.doc: well-formed, but not a chart

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_MISPLACED_CONSTRUCT
constants.doc: <else > before an <elseif >; <param > with <content >

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_CONFLICTING_ATTRIBUTE
constants.doc: both `event` and `eventexpr`

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_BAD_VALUE
constants.doc: a duration, a boolean, an ID list

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_FOREIGN_CONTENT
constants.doc: SCXML 4.10 content, no lowering (ADR 0046)

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_SRC_UNRESOLVED
constants.doc: a src= and no resolver

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_LIMIT
constants.doc: a bound this codec enforces was reached

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE
constants.doc: encode: the spec has no form in this syntax

ta_chart_expression_printer_vtable.doc: Renders TA_EXPRESSION_HOST back to source during an encode. A spec decoded from a document carries only TA_EXPRESSION_SOURCE and needs none; a spec built from host handles is TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE without it.

ta_chart_lowering_vtable.doc: Lowers SCXML 4.10 platform-specific executable content to a <send > to a registered I/O processor, the only form core has for it (ADR 0046). `element` is the element as written. Returning TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND refuses the document, which SCXML A.2 permits. An absent adapter refuses every such element: skipping one would silently drop behaviour the author wrote.

ta_chart_position.doc:
======================================================================== Chart codecs (ADR 0053)

A codec turns bytes into a ta_scxml_spec and back. Core defines the adapter and the in-memory form and links no parser: SCXML XML, a JSON encoding and a tree-sitter grammar are all codecs, and none is in core.

Core calls a codec only from ta_definition_import() and ta_definition_encode(). An embedder may also decode and then compile with ta_definition_compile_spec() itself.

ta_chart_src_resolver_vtable.doc: Resolves <data src> and <script src> during a decode: the one route to the outside world, and the embedder's, never core's and never the codec's. For <script > the bytes are source text. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when `src` names nothing the resolver knows. An <invoke src> is not fetched: it is a URI the invoker interprets at run time (SCXML 6.4), and stays in the spec.

ta_datamodel_declare_params.doc:
Named top-level data bindings (SCXML <data >). `name` is the author's data ID, borrowed for the call. declare() creates the binding with the data model's uninitialized representation; set_named() installs an initializer's value. Late binding declares every binding at bootstrap and sets each one only when its state is first entered (ADR 0032).

`bound` may be null. declare() sets `*bound` when the instance's binding already supplies a value for `name` (e.g. <param >s passed to an invoked child); the core then skips that binding's initializer.

ta_datamodel_foreach_snapshot_params.doc: <foreach >: foreach_snapshot evaluates `array` once and returns a shallow copy and its length; the core keeps the snapshot while iterating. foreach_bind assigns item `index` of the snapshot to the `item` variable and, when index_name.ptr is non-null, the index to that variable.

ta_datamodel_import_content_params.doc: Imports literal <content > or <data > content into a legal data-model value.

ta_datamodel_prepare_definition_params.doc: Prepares one compiled definition for a data model. `expressions` is the definition's expression table, indexed by ta_expr_id. It is borrowed and remains valid until destroy_definition() for the same `shared` state, so the adapter may keep the pointer instead of copying. The adapter never sees the compiled definition itself.

ta_datamodel_value_text_params.doc: Conversions the SCXML `*expr` attribute forms need. value_text reads an evaluated value as text (eventexpr, typeexpr, sendidexpr, srcexpr, delayexpr, targetexpr); `*out` is borrowed from `value` and valid while it is retained, so core can parse a target URI out of it and keep the named address a send needs (ADR 0044). text_value makes a value from text, e.g. a generated send or invoke ID stored through idlocation.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The SCXML data-model name this adapter implements, e.g. "null" or "ecmascript". Compared with ta_scxml_spec.datamodel at compile time.

ta_definition_compile_params.doc:
Compile a sentinel-terminated SCXML specification into an immutable definition.

The compiler resolves state IDs and event descriptors, interns named send events, I/O processor and invoker types, and literal send and invoke IDs, validates the complete tree, and copies all data it retains. Thus the specification may be a nested compound literal with automatic storage. Every optional field is absent when zero-initialized; no field takes a runtime identifier such as `ta_expr_id`, `ta_send_id`, or `ta_atom`.

ta_definition_export_params.doc:
Rebuilds the author-level spec of a registered definition (ADR 0042). Arrays and joined event names are allocated in `arena`; other text and expressions are borrowed from the definition and the system. Host expressions are the definition's retained handles, not retained again. The result stays valid until the arena is reset or the definition is freed, whichever comes first.

Export is faithful: compiling the exported spec yields the same revision as the original. `identity` is null when the definition was fingerprinted and points to the definition's explicit identity otherwise. Empty lists are exported as null, except that a handler's `actions` is never null.

TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND: no existing definition has this ID. A retired definition exports until it is freed.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The author's state ID, as `ta_definition_state` reports it.

ta_definition_id.doc: A registered definition: its table slot in the low 32 bits and the slot's generation in the high 32 bits (ADR 0043). Zero is never a valid ID. A freed definition's ID goes stale and never names another definition.

ta_definition_identity.doc: Process-independent identity of one exact immutable definition revision. `family` is the stable logical statechart family; `revision` is an opaque fingerprint copied/owned by the compiled definition.  Any change that can alter interpretation of a session image must produce a different revision.

ta_definition_inspection.doc: A read-only view of one registered definition. Text and the adapter are borrowed from the system and stay valid while the definition exists (a retired definition exists until its last resident actor is gone).

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: The exact revision (ADR 0028, ADR 0038).

fields.name: document_name
fields.doc: The <scxml name> attribute, which _name reads; empty when absent.

fields.name: datamodel
fields.doc: The adapter instance the definition was compiled with. `self` identifies the instance and `v->name` the SCXML data-model name. Use it to identify the adapter; never call its operations.

fields.name: binding
fields.doc: TA_SCXML_BINDING_EARLY or TA_SCXML_BINDING_LATE, never DEFAULT.

fields.name: state_count
fields.doc: States readable with ta_definition_state().

fields.name: retired
fields.doc: True after the definition is retired (ADR 0043).

fields.name: actor_count
fields.doc: Resident actors using this definition, unpublished replacements included.

fields.name: actor_fixed_bytes
fields.doc: Bytes the core allocates for each actor of this definition before it processes events: the actor record, session storage (configuration and history), and the data-model instance. Excludes queues, the sparse state of invoked actors, and memory the data-model adapter allocates itself. A measurement: it may change between releases.

fields.name: definition_bytes
fields.doc: Bytes of the definition's own storage (its arena). A measurement.

ta_delayed_send_info.doc: One pending delayed send owned by an actor (ADR 0054). `destination` is the resolved target for the built-in SCXML processor; custom processors receive `target` and leave `destination` unused. `submitted` means the router refused the send once and it waits to be offered again (ADR 0026, ADR 0040). Everything is borrowed; retain `target` and `data` with ta_value_retain() to keep them past the synchronization window.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_NAME
constants.doc: _event.name, dotted.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_TYPE
constants.doc: _event.type: "platform", "internal", or "external".

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_SENDID
constants.doc: _event.sendid: the author's send ID, or the generated one.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_ORIGIN
constants.doc: _event.origin, a URI that can be used as a send target.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_ORIGINTYPE
constants.doc: _event.origintype, the URI of the processor for origin.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_INVOKEID
constants.doc: _event.invokeid.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_SESSION_ID
constants.doc: _sessionid.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_SESSION_NAME
constants.doc: _name: the <scxml > name attribute.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_SCXML_IO_LOCATION
constants.doc: _ioprocessors: the SCXML Event I/O Processor's location for this session.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_SCXML_IO_TYPE
constants.doc: _ioprocessors: the SCXML Event I/O Processor's type URI.

ta_dm_text_kind.doc: Text of the SCXML system variables, for data models that expose them (SCXML 5.10). Each field is formatted into the caller's buffer following the list-output convention: `*needed` always receives the size including the terminating NUL, and a too-small buffer yields TA_ERR_NOMEM without writing. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND means the field has no value, e.g. no event has been processed yet, or the current event has no send ID or origin.

fields.name: budget
fields.doc: Must be nonzero; limits synchronous host callbacks in this call.

ta_expression.doc: A frontend expression retained by a compiled definition. Source expressions are copied by the definition compiler. Host expressions are retained and released through their adapter; for example, a Node-API adapter retains a napi_ref rather than a callback-scoped napi_value.

ta_external_delivery.doc: A fully normalized event destined for another SCXML external event queue.

fields.name: v
fields.doc: Null uninstalls the router.

constants.name: TA_EXTERNAL_EVENT_ACCEPTED
constants.doc: Delivery was accepted; an asynchronous router copied borrowed fields.

constants.name: TA_EXTERNAL_EVENT_RETRY
constants.doc: Nothing was accepted; core retains and retries the delivery.

constants.name: TA_EXTERNAL_EVENT_ERROR
constants.doc: Nothing was accepted; fault describes a communication failure.

ta_fault.doc:
invoke_id is TA_INVOKE_ID_NONE unless an invoked child generated the event.

A receiver of a fault owns its data; the message is borrowed.

ta_invoke_report_kind.doc: Asynchronous outcome of a previously successful invoker start.  EVENT and DONE enter the actor's external-event flow.  UNAVAILABLE retires the service and appends error.communication.invoke. <id >.unavailable to the internal queue.

ta_invoke_request.doc: One invocation to start. `type` is the resolved invoker type; the SCXML aliases "scxml" and "http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml" are normalized to "http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/". `src` is the evaluated src/srcexpr, `data` the evaluated ` <content expr>`, and `params` the data model's aggregate of <param >/namelist values; each is empty (null vtable) when absent. A literal <content > is not imported: it arrives as `content`, the bytes the chart holds, with `content_type` its media type (empty when nothing said), and interpreting it is the invoker's business (ADR 0053, SCXML 6.4.2). Values and bytes are borrowed for the call. A service for an SCXML session spawns its child with ta_actor_spawn() and a `parent` of {parent, invoke_id}; the core then routes `#_ <invokeid >` sends, autoforwarding, and done.invoke itself.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: start must not report reentrantly through ta_actor_report_invoke().

ta_log_record.doc:
======================================================================== Logging

SCXML <log > (SCXML 4.7): a label and an optional value, with an implementation-dependent rendering. The record carries the evaluated value rather than text, as ta_send does, so the host renders it with the data model it already owns (ADR 0045).

fields.name: source
fields.doc: The actor that ran the <log >.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: <log label>; empty when the author wrote none.

fields.name: has_value
fields.doc: False when the <log > has no expr, or when evaluating it failed.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Borrowed for the call; retain it to keep it (ADR 0006).

fields.name: v
fields.doc: Null uninstalls the sink; <log > then only evaluates its expression.

ta_log_sink_vtable.doc: Writing a log has no result: SCXML 4.7 requires <log > to have no effect on document interpretation, so a sink cannot fail the action.

ta_named_value.doc: One <param >: `name` is the author's parameter name, borrowed for the call.

ta_scxml_binding_kind.doc: Zero selects the SCXML default, early binding.

ta_scxml_data_spec.doc: SCXML ` <data src>` is resolved by the importer, which performs any I/O and passes the result as TA_SCXML_VALUE_CONTENT; the core performs no I/O.

ta_scxml_done_data_spec.doc: Exactly one of content or params may be present, as required by SCXML.

ta_scxml_handler_spec.doc:
One <onentry > or <onexit > handler. SCXML 3.8 and 3.9 require each handler to be a separate block of executable content: when an action fails, the rest of that handler is skipped, and the handlers after it still run. A state lists its handlers in document order.

`actions` is required, because a null `actions` terminates the handler list. An empty handler (` <onentry />`) points to an empty action list, `(const ta_scxml_action_spec[]){{0}}`, or is left out.

ta_scxml_id_kind.doc: The `id` / `idlocation` pair of <send > and <invoke >. A literal ID is the author's string; LOCATION stores the ID the processor generates each time the element executes. A zero-initialized value is absent, in which case the processor still generates an ID but does not store it.

ta_scxml_invoke_spec.doc: `type` names a registered invoker (`type` / `typeexpr`); `src` is the `src` / `srcexpr` pair; `data` is the inline <content >. SCXML `namelist` is lowered to `params` as for <send >.

ta_scxml_send_spec.doc: `type` names a registered I/O processor (`type` / `typeexpr`); absent selects the built-in SCXML Event I/O Processor. A literal `delay` is an SCXML duration such as "500ms" or "5s" and is compiled to logical milliseconds; a `delayexpr` is evaluated when the send executes. SCXML `namelist` is lowered to `params`: each name becomes a parameter whose value is a TA_SCXML_VALUE_LOCATION of the same name.

fields.name: datamodel
fields.doc: The <scxml > `datamodel` attribute: the data model this document requires. Absent means no requirement. The compiler returns TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when it differs from the adapter's name.

fields.name: script
fields.doc: The <scxml > <script > child (SCXML 3.2.2, 5.8), absent when zero. Each session runs it once at initialization: after early-bound data is initialized and before the initial transition is taken. A runtime failure queues error.execution. <script src> is fetched by the importer and passed as source text; the core performs no I/O.

ta_scxml_string_kind.doc: An SCXML attribute pair of the form `x` / `xexpr`: either literal text written by the author or an expression evaluated when the element executes. A zero-initialized value is absent.

fields.name: media_type
fields.doc: What these bytes are, as the codec that produced them knows it; the decoding codec's info.name. Empty when nothing said. Opaque to core.

ta_send.doc: One send to a host I/O processor. `data` is the evaluated ` <content expr>`, namelist or <param >s; `content` is a literal <content >, delivered as the bytes the chart holds and not imported into the data model (ADR 0053). `content_type` is the literal's media type, empty when nothing said. At most one of `data` and `content` is present. Everything is borrowed for the call.

ta_state_info.doc: Static facts about one state of a registered definition. `id` is the author's state ID and is borrowed from the system. `parent` is TA_STATE_NONE for top-level states. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND ends iteration over state IDs 0, 1, 2, ... in document order; it is also the result when the definition ID is unknown or stale. A retired definition is readable until it is freed.

ta_state_kind.doc: The kind of a compiled state, as reported by ta_definition_state().

ta_time.doc: Monotonic logical time in milliseconds, supplied by the embedder.

ta_tree.doc: Storage for dynamically authored specification trees. A tree owns all allocations made through it until ta_tree_destroy(). Its first allocation failure is retained and reported by ta_tree_result(); subsequent writes are ignored so import code can report one result at its outer boundary.

ta_tree_list.doc: A temporary, type-erased child list owned by a ta_tree.

functions.name: ta_arena_allocator
functions.doc: An allocator that draws from `arena` and whose free() does nothing, so an arena can back anything that wants a ta_allocator (ADR 0053). What it allocates lives until the arena is reset or destroyed.

functions.name: ta_external_delivery_clone
functions.doc: Deep-copies a named destination and clones event data.

functions.name: ta_scxml_target_parse
functions.doc:
The SCXML Event I/O Processor target URIs (ADR 0044). Core owns the grammar, so a literal `target`, an evaluated `targetexpr`, and the text core writes for `$_event.origin` agree by construction:

#_internal                 the sender's own internal queue #_parent                   the invoking parent session #_scxml_ <session >          a session by its runtime ID #_actor_ <family >/ <name >    a named actor by its logical address #_ <invokeid >               an invocation of the sending session

A session URI whose text is not a session ID names no session: it parses as runtime actor 0, which never exists, so a send to it is inaccessible (SCXML C.1) rather than invalid. TA_ERR_INVALID means an invalid target, which a send reports as error.execution.

A named address borrows its family and name from `text`, which must stay valid for as long as the target is used.

functions.name: ta_scxml_target_format
functions.doc: The URI of a target. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when its kind has no URI.

functions.name: ta_send_id_parse
functions.doc:
Send IDs as text (ADR 0048). A literal ` <send id>` is the author's text; a generated ID is `#_send. <n >`, the sending actor's counter. Core writes this text for `idlocation` and `_event.sendid` and reads it back for ` <cancel sendidexpr>`, so the two forms name the same send by construction: a host holding a `ta_send_id`, such as an I/O processor looking at `ta_send.send_id`, can render the text its chart holds, and a host holding that text can name the send core knows.

Parsing the generated form always succeeds, whether or not such a send exists, as a session URI does. A literal ID must already be interned in this system, since no send of it can carry text it has never seen: otherwise TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND. TA_ERR_INVALID means the text is no send ID at all, such as an empty string.

functions.name: ta_send_id_format
functions.doc: The text of a send ID, following the buffer convention: `*needed` receives the size including the terminating NUL, and a too-small buffer yields TA_ERR_NOMEM without writing, so a zero capacity is a size query. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the send has no ID.

functions.name: ta_dm_host_in_state
functions.doc: Queries available to a data-model adapter while core calls into it.

functions.name: ta_dm_host_find_state
functions.doc: The state of the running definition with this author ID, for In() (ADR 0049). TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the chart has no such state: SCXML B.1 makes In() of it simply false, so an adapter answers that without a lookup of its own.

functions.name: ta_dm_host_state_name
functions.doc: The author's ID of a state; TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND ends iteration over 0, 1, 2, ...

functions.name: ta_actor_report_invoke
functions.doc: Externally synchronize this call; do not call it reentrantly from start.

functions.name: ta_tree_init
functions.doc: Initialize storage used while dynamically constructing a specification.

functions.name: ta_actor_prepare_replacement
functions.doc: Creates an unpublished actor and holds bootstrap effects until activation.

functions.name: ta_actor_activate_replacement
functions.doc: Atomically replaces the route, then releases held effects in SCXML order.

functions.name: ta_actor_unload
functions.doc: Evicts a named actor without terminating it. The image must be a fresh capture of actor; TA_ERR_STALE means the actor changed after capture.

functions.name: ta_actor_load
functions.doc: Restores an unloaded named actor and atomically republishes its route.

functions.name: ta_actor_reconstruct
functions.doc: Reconstructs an image under a fresh runtime ID without reading or changing the actor directory. For a named image, the logical self-address is kept; sends to that address follow the directory's current route.

functions.name: ta_actor_remove_unloaded
functions.doc: Releases the name of an unloaded actor; the host then deletes its checkpoint.

functions.name: ta_actor_publish_completion
functions.doc: Retries an invoked child's completion after TA_ERR_BUSY. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND retires it when the parent invocation was already cancelled.

functions.name: ta_system_visit_actors
functions.doc: Visits every resident actor once, invoked children included, with the same view ta_actor_inspect() gives for it. The walk stops at the first visit that answers anything but TA_OK and returns that result, so an inspector can end it early; a null `visit` is TA_ERR_INVALID. The order of the walk is not part of the contract.

functions.name: ta_actor_datamodel_root
functions.doc: The data model's inspection root (its `inspect` operation). Release it with ta_value_release(). TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when the adapter has none.

functions.name: ta_definition_find_state
functions.doc: The state of a definition with this author ID: the inverse of ta_definition_state (ADR 0049). TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the definition has no such state, which is a question, not a failure.

functions.name: ta_definition_inspect
functions.doc: TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the ID names no existing definition: never registered, freed after retirement, or stale.

functions.name: ta_session_image_next_deadline
functions.doc: Returns TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the captured actor owns no delayed send.

functions.name: ta_system_set_external_event_router
functions.doc: Installs the scheduler for normalized external SCXML-session events.

functions.name: ta_system_register_definition
functions.doc: Registration takes ownership of definition only when it returns TA_OK.

functions.name: ta_system_find_definition
functions.doc: The registered, non-retired definition with exactly this identity; family and revision are compared bytewise. When several match, the most recently registered wins. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when none matches.

functions.name: ta_system_retire_definition
functions.doc: Ends a definition's availability (ADR 0043). ta_actor_spawn() and ta_actor_prepare_replacement() naming it fail with TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND, and ta_system_find_definition() skips it. Resident actors that use it keep running, and ta_definition_inspect(), ta_definition_state(), and ta_definition_export() keep working. The system frees the definition (its data-model state, its storage, and its ID) when no resident actor uses it: here if none does, otherwise when the last one is destroyed. Idempotent: retiring a retired definition, even one already freed, returns TA_OK. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the ID was never issued.

functions.name: ta_system_register_io
functions.doc: The atom returned by ta_system_scxml_io_type() is reserved.

functions.name: ta_system_set_log_sink
functions.doc: Installs where <log > goes; without one, a <log > only evaluates its expr.

functions.name: ta_system_atom_text
functions.doc: The text an atom interns (ADR 0049), borrowed from the system's atom table and valid while the system is. Atoms are system-local (ADR 0007): one of another system is TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND, not undefined. This is the inverse of ta_system_intern_atom, so a host that is handed `ta_send.io_type` or `ta_invoke_request.type` can say what it was given.

functions.name: ta_system_invoke_id_text
functions.doc: The text of an invocation's ID (ADR 0049): the author's ` <invoke id>`, or the ` <stateid >. <platformid >` core generated for one without. It is what `done.invoke. <id >` names and what the `#_ <invokeid >` target spells, so a host holding `ta_active_invoke.id` can say which invocation it has. Borrowed from the system. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND for an ID it never issued.

functions.name: ta_system_scxml_io_type
functions.doc: Returns the built-in SCXML Event I/O Processor's system-local type atom.

functions.name: ta_system_next_deadline
functions.doc: TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND means that no resident delayed send is pending.
